## Findings
- claim-1: \(\Lambda\) has integral Schur basis \(\{s_\lambda\}\), and \(I_{r,q}=\operatorname{Span}_{\mathbb Z}\{s_\lambda:\lambda\nsubseteq q^r\}\) is an ideal with \(\Lambda/I_{r,q}\cong H^*(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,r+q})\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-218]
- claim-2: The map \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\) is a ring involution of \(\Lambda\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 481-485]
- claim-3: For all \(r,q\ge1\), \(\omega(I_{r,q})=I_{q,r}\); consequently \(\omega\) induces a graded integral ring isomorphism \[ \omega_{r,q}:\Lambda/I_{r,q}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda/I_{q,r}, \qquad \overline{s_\lambda}\mapsto\overline{s_{\lambda'}}, \] whose inverse is \(\omega_{q,r}\).
## Strategy
By [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 481-485], \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\) is a ring involution of \(\Lambda\). It is integral because it permutes the integral Schur basis, and graded because \(|\lambda'|=|\lambda|\).

A partition \(\lambda\) lies in \(q^r\) iff \(\lambda_1\le q\) and \(\ell(\lambda)\le r\). Equivalently,
\[
(\lambda')_1=\ell(\lambda)\le r,\qquad \ell(\lambda')=\lambda_1\le q,
\]
so \(\lambda'\subseteq r^q\). Thus conjugation bijects partitions outside \(q^r\) with those outside \(r^q\). Using
\[
I_{r,q}=\bigoplus_{\lambda\nsubseteq q^r}\mathbb Zs_\lambda
\]
([doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-218]) gives basiswise
\[
\omega(I_{r,q})=I_{q,r}.
\]
Hence \(\omega\) descends to a graded integral ring isomorphism
\[
\omega_{r,q}:\Lambda/I_{r,q}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda/I_{q,r},
\qquad \bar s_\lambda\mapsto\bar s_{\lambda'},
\]
with inverse \(\omega_{q,r}\), since \((\lambda')'=\lambda\).

For \(r=1\), \((k)\subseteq q^1\) iff \(k\le q\), and \((k)'=(1^k)\subseteq1^q\). For \(q=1\), \((1^k)\subseteq1^r\) iff \(k\le r\), and \((1^k)'=(k)\subseteq r^1\). Thus both boundary cases satisfy the same argument.

The requested claim-3 certificate is established. No finite \(G_L\)-to-\(G_R\) computation was used.
